name: Pasta ai Quattro Formaggi
steps: Check that all four cheeses are made with vegetarian coagulants. Cut the mozzarella and fontina-style cheese into small pieces, crumble the blue cheese and finely grate the hard cheese. Small pieces melt evenly without overheating the sauce.

Bring the measured water to a rolling boil in a large pot. Add 6 g salt and the penne, stir, then cook to the pack's al dente point, usually 10–12 minutes. A cut piece should have no dry centre but still feel firm. Reserve 250 ml starchy cooking water before draining.

While the pasta cooks, warm the milk and butter in a wide pan over low heat until the butter melts; do not boil. Add the mozzarella, fontina-style cheese and blue cheese in two additions, stirring gently until just melted and smooth. Turn off the heat and stir in half the hard cheese.

Add the drained hot penne to the warm sauce. Toss over very low heat for up to 1 minute, adding reserved pasta water a few spoonfuls at a time until the sauce is silky and coats the penne. If it begins to split or clump, take the pan off the heat and stir in a little more warm pasta water.

Season with black pepper and taste before adding the remaining 1 g salt; the cheeses may already provide enough. Divide into four warm bowls, scatter over the remaining hard cheese and serve immediately while creamy.
tips: A mild melting cheese, a soft cheese, a small amount of blue cheese and a hard finishing cheese give balance. Keep the sauce below a simmer so it stays smooth.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
